rationale: Averages discard within-episode feature variation; a distributional episode representation can retain heterogeneous dorsal observations without requiring a teacher or deleting events.
encoder: Same fully frozen ImageNet ResNet18 for original letterboxed RGB/depth; per-frame L2 normalisation
bag: Same deterministic maximum 12 unique decoded RGB representatives per episode, no padding, no quality filtering
representation: Project each normalised frame embedding on fixed random unit directions; interpolate the empirical quantile function at 16 fixed midpoints; flatten and divide by sqrt(64*16). This finite feature map is an approximation, not the exact sliced Wasserstein distance.
joint: Concatenate normalised RGB and depth frame features with sqrt(0.5) scaling, then project in 1024 dimensions; filename pairing is not claimed as independently verified sensor synchronisation
shuffled_control: Fixed different permutation of depth frames inside each episode, preserves each modality marginal and episode label; no cross-animal transfer, all mappings logged
SVR: C=1/alpha, epsilon=0.1; RBF bandwidth is training pairwise median squared distance times scale; validation MAE selects a single grid point
novelty: An event-level application and controlled pairing/heterogeneity evaluation; distribution regression and sliced Wasserstein kernels are established approaches, not invented here
